subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the durable memory write resolver live in memory-core, memory-wiki, memory-lancedb, or a new plugin SDK/active-memory contract before implementation starts?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the durable schema owner, conflict semantics, provenance requirements, and operator review UX are product and ownership decisions rather than a safe mechanical repair.

options.title: Design active-memory contract first
options.body: Use memory-core or a new active-memory SDK seam as the owner for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history before coding the resolver.

options.title: Route through memory-wiki
options.body: Treat structured claims, contradictions, evidence, and dashboards as memory-wiki responsibilities while keeping memory-core focused on files, search, promotion, and dreaming.

options.title: Defer durable resolver
options.body: Keep current Markdown, LanceDB, and wiki layers while collecting more production examples before committing to a durable write API.

recommendation.title: Design active-memory contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core or a new active-memory SDK seam as the owner for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history before coding the resolver.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest inspected signal across recent memory-core maintenance, memory-wiki documentation, and the core-versus-plugin product boundary.
